key_insight: Biomedical reranking made the right clinical evidence appear earlier in long-note QA, improving retrieval more than final answer accuracy.
clinical_relevance: For longitudinal clinical notes, better evidence ordering can help retrieval-augmented systems answer patient-specific questions more reliably.
method: PubMedBERT dense retrieval + BM25 lexical retrieval
MedCPT cross-encoder reranking with Qwen3-8B answer generation
evidence_signal: In 1,000 QA pairs from 200 bariatric surgery patients, Hit@10 rose from 46.6% to 60.6% and MRR from 0.2371 to 0.3252, while answer correctness increased from 44.8% to 48.6%.
watch_item: Retrieval gains did not translate proportionally into answer gains, so context-window limits and downstream generation quality remain important implementation concerns.
paper_title: Evaluating Biomedical Reranking for LLM-Based Question Answering over Longitudinal Clinical Notes
